correctness.rationale: The exact projected residual dynamics close as a two-state positive matrix for every admissible parameter, allowing Perron–Frobenius and the exact covariance identity; an elementary squared-difference identity gives the sign and a monotonic scalar maximization gives the sharp 1/8 bound. Exact rational trajectory enumeration (7,650 paths), 19,900 spectral grid checks and near-extremal tests executed successfully. Finite checks do not serve as infinite proofs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General stochastic-coordinate contraction bounds and E-optimal one-step probabilities give upper bounds but do not identify the exact asymptotic actual expectation relative to the new restricted-subspace mean nor its global discrepancy. The motivating theorem explicitly assumes nonnegative covariance and thus does not assert coverage of the negative-covariance regime.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text source checks show the 2026 RBSCD Theorem 4.3 assumes nonnegative covariance and does not establish this universal eventual sign reversal for biased two-column sampling or its sharp rate gap. The most relevant published two-dimensional result covers uniformly sampled delayed iterations and a different metric; another optimizes worst-case one-step contraction. Full comparable claim implications rather than titles were evaluated. Older equivalent Markov-product results remain an explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: The derivation uses classical 2x2 Perron theory and projector geometry; exact-equivalence formulations could exist in older alternating-projections or Markov switching literature.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a complete, nontrivial parameter-wide sign characterization of a hypothesis used by a new non-worst-case coordinate-sampling analysis, quantifies its maximum asymptotic optimism by a sharp 1/8, and exhibits the limitation even at condition number tending to one. It does not claim the original conditional theorem is false, or that a two-coordinate model proves general batch behavior.
